props.title: Face

sections.content: **Face** (1997) represents a pivotal moment in Japanese New Wave cinema, directed by Juzo Itami's protégé Sakamoto Junji. The film follows a woman disfigured in an acid attack, brilliantly played by Naomi Fujiyama, exploring themes of identity and social stigma that echo earlier masterpieces like **Eyes Without a Face** (1960) and **The Elephant Man** (1980). Its unflinching examination of beauty standards in Japanese society opened doors for later films tackling similar themes, like **Helter Skelter** (2012). Eyes Without a Face|1960|A French horror classic about a surgeon's desperate attempts to restore his daughter's disfigured face|Criterion The Elephant Man|1980|David Lynch's haunting portrayal of John Merrick, exploring humanity beneath physical appearance|HBO Max Mask|1985|True story of Rocky Dennis, a teen with a rare disfiguring condition, starring Cher|Netflix

The film's technical brilliance lies in its intimate cinematography, with close-ups that force viewers to confront their own prejudices about facial difference. This technique would later influence works like **Under the Skin** (2013) and **The Skin I Live In** (2011), both of which deal with physical transformation and society's obsession with appearance. Sakamoto's direction creates an atmosphere of uncomfortable intimacy that makes the audience question their own biases. SUBHEAD: Social Commentary and Identity

**Face** (1997) sparked a wave of Japanese films examining social outcasts and identity, paving the way for works like **All About Lily Chou-Chou** (2001) and **Suicide Club** (2001). Its exploration of isolation and alienation in modern Japanese society connects strongly to contemporary issues of social pressure and conformity, themes later explored in **Perfect Blue** (1997) and **Tokyo Sonata** (2008). Perfect Blue|1997|Satoshi Kon's psychological thriller about identity and fame in Japanese society|Prime The Skin I Live In|2011|Almodóvar's twisted tale of revenge, identity, and transformation|HBO Max Under the Skin|2013|Scarlett Johansson stars as an alien examining human identity and appearance|Hulu
